test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 29 Aug 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In which year was The Indian Toll Act passed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1851.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The "Indian Tolls Act, 1851," as it is called, was passed on July 4th of that year. Governments** are now permitted to charge tolls on these routes and specific bridges thanks to the passage of the law.
 
• The **legislation covers the areas that, as of July 4, 1851, **were under the council-mandated rule of** the Governor and Presidency of Fort William of the Bengal **region and the **Governor of Fort St. George's presidency.**
 
• Any road or bridge that has been built or will be repaired at the** government's expense** may be subject to tolls at whatever rates the government deems appropriate.
 
• **The government may also assign responsibility **for managing the toll collection to whomever it deems appropriate, and any individuals working in this capacity will be subject to the same obligations as those who **work in the actual toll collection.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Indian Tolls Act 1901**:

 
 
• **The Indian Tolls (Army & Air Force) Act, 1901** is a law that was passed by the **Indian Parliament** and put forth by **the Ministry of Defence** to address the exemption of toll charges for regular** armed forces,** including all family **members of Indian Armed Forces **extending from **Indian Army to Central Armed Police Forces, **where applicable.
 
• The **requirements of sections 3 and 4 **were later removed from **the act by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways**, and those only "on duty" would be entitled to the exemption, which does not apply to the retired individual.
 
• This was done in response to **new legislation and policy formulation.**
